$meta.generated: docs/product/design/tokens.css is generated from this file by ops/scripts/build-design-tokens.mjs — edit the JSON, never the CSS
$meta.note: Semantic roles only. No token names a hue, a screen, or a component; a role may be re-pointed without renaming a call site. Light is warm paper, dark is neutral; every state and presence role now declares the quiet fill it is actually painted on, so the contrast check sees the ground that ships.

bg.role: the window canvas behind everything — warm paper, not a cool grey

elevated.role: menus, popovers, sheets, the command palette

sunken.role: code blocks, wells, inset scroll regions

border.role: separators between rows and around inputs

border-strong.role: separator and rule: table rules, list dividers, the hairline under a toolbar. A separator is decorative under 1.4.11 and is not held to 3:1 — it sits at ~1.8:1 on every ground by design, because a rule that meets 3:1 reads as a border. Anything that BOUNDS A CONTROL uses border-control instead.

border-control.role: the outline of a discrete control where the outline is what identifies it: secondary and bordered buttons, unselected filter chips, segmented controls, the composer field, select menus, the new-rows pill. Held to 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11) on every ground it can sit on, because the warm light palette separates bg, surface and sunken by under 1.2:1 — so in light mode the outline is the only thing distinguishing a control from the page, and it has to carry that alone.
border-control.apple: separatorColor (raised: Apple's own bordered controls rely on a fill difference this palette does not have)

text-secondary.role: metadata that must still be read: timestamps, counts, actor ids

text-tertiary.role: placeholders and de-emphasised hints; never the only carrier of meaning, and never on a tinted fill — only on bg, surface or elevated

accent.role: the one interactive colour: links, selected tab, primary button fill. Pinned as the brand colour; controlAccentColor drives only the controls Apple draws itself

accent-hover.role: hover and pressed state of an accent surface

accent-quiet.role: selection and emphasis ground: a selected row, your own turn in the transcript, the selection bar. LEGAL INK ON IT, and nothing else: text-primary, text-secondary, accent, agent as text; ok, degraded, failed and stale as a GLYPH only (they clear 3:1 and not 4.5:1). text-tertiary is illegal on it — 4.17:1 light, 4.06:1 dark — as is any state colour used as words. This list exists because the same pair has now failed twice: a selection ground re-inks everything inside it, so every role that can appear in a row has to be checked against it, not just the ones a designer happens to think of.

on-accent.role: text and glyphs on an accent fill

agent.role: the agent-sourced tint — marks a string an agent wrote, as data

agent-quiet.role: agent-sourced background wash: quoted tool output, agent comment

entity-person.role: ENTITY HUE — a person — an @mention resolving to a People/ page. Hue here says WHAT KIND OF THING a chip points at, never how urgent it is. Only ever ink on its own *-quiet fill; never a background, never a border, never text on bg/surface. Urgency is carried by weight and fill (priority) and by the state tokens (something is wrong) — three channels that must not be mixed.

entity-person-quiet.role: the chip fill behind entity-person. Sits in the same band as the other quiet fills (~1.17:1 on bg light, ~1.48:1 dark) so an entity chip never outweighs a state chip.

entity-note.role: ENTITY HUE — a note, a page, a document link — anything in the vault. Hue here says WHAT KIND OF THING a chip points at, never how urgent it is. Only ever ink on its own *-quiet fill; never a background, never a border, never text on bg/surface. Urgency is carried by weight and fill (priority) and by the state tokens (something is wrong) — three channels that must not be mixed.

entity-note-quiet.role: the chip fill behind entity-note. Sits in the same band as the other quiet fills (~1.17:1 on bg light, ~1.48:1 dark) so an entity chip never outweighs a state chip.

entity-project.role: ENTITY HUE — a project or an area. Hue here says WHAT KIND OF THING a chip points at, never how urgent it is. Only ever ink on its own *-quiet fill; never a background, never a border, never text on bg/surface. Urgency is carried by weight and fill (priority) and by the state tokens (something is wrong) — three channels that must not be mixed.

entity-project-quiet.role: the chip fill behind entity-project. Sits in the same band as the other quiet fills (~1.17:1 on bg light, ~1.48:1 dark) so an entity chip never outweighs a state chip.

ok.role: check passed, run succeeded, thread resolved

ok-quiet.role: the fill an ok chip is actually painted on — declared so the checker sees the ground that ships

degraded.role: answering but not healthy: stale collector, fallback tier, queued over cap

degraded-quiet.role: the fill a degraded chip is actually painted on — declared so the checker sees the ground that ships

failed-quiet.role: the fill a failed chip is actually painted on — declared so the checker sees the ground that ships

absent.role: not configured — a fact, not a fault

absent-quiet.role: the fill an absent chip is actually painted on — declared so the checker sees the ground that ships

stale.role: was answering and has not lately: the reading on screen is the last one, and its age is on the row

stale-quiet.role: the fill a stale chip is actually painted on — declared so the checker sees the ground that ships

presence-working-quiet.role: the tinted fill behind a working presence chip

presence-queued.role: claimed or waiting behind a cap

presence-queued-quiet.role: the tinted fill behind a queued presence chip

presence-idle-quiet.role: the tinted fill behind an idle presence chip

presence-interrupted-quiet.role: the tinted fill behind an interrupted presence chip

presence-over-cap-quiet.role: the tinted fill behind an over-cap presence chip

presence-blocked.role: waiting on you or another agent

presence-blocked-quiet.role: the tinted fill behind a blocked presence chip

destructive.role: the fill of a destructive control — Decline, Revoke, Rotate. A fill, not a foreground: failed is the foreground role

on-destructive.role: text and glyphs on a destructive fill

affirmative.role: the fill of the affirming action — Approve, Add, Connect. A fill, where `ok` is the foreground role for a state: a button that starts something is not a status report about it

on-affirmative.role: text and glyphs on an affirmative fill

$meta.family: SF on Apple platforms; on the web the system stack resolves to SF on Apple, Segoe UI Variable on Windows, Roboto on Android, Cantarell/Ubuntu on Linux. No webfont is ever loaded.
$meta.stack: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, system-ui, 'Segoe UI Variable Text', 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Cantarell, 'Helvetica Neue', sans-serif
$meta.mono: ui-monospace, SFMono-Regular, 'SF Mono', Menlo, Consolas, 'Liberation Mono', monospace
$meta.serif: "New York", Charter, 'Iowan Old Style', Georgia, serif — AGENT PROSE ONLY. The faces are NAMED rather than left to the generic ui-serif, because ui-serif resolves to Times in a browser and Times is what made agent prose read as unformatted system text. New York is Apple's companion serif to SF; Charter and Iowan Old Style catch older Apple platforms; Georgia catches everything else. The chain stops at Georgia so Times is never reached. Every face is a system face, so P7 holds: no webfont is ever loaded.

$meta.note: Assistant and agent reply prose only — never a control, a label, or a feed row. It is a separate group from `type` because a reply is the one place in the system optimised for DENSITY: the longest text on the smallest screen, read once, at length. Everything else is optimised for scanning.
$meta.why-not-body: `body` is 17pt (Apple's .body) and correct for controls and first-read chrome. A 200-word reply set at 17/1.5 inside a 390pt bubble runs about six words a line and pushes the previous turn off-screen. The reply group drops to 15pt on a phone and 16pt on a Mac, tightens the line box to 1.45, and replaces the blank-line paragraph break with a 12px margin — roughly a third more words on screen at the same measured contrast.
$meta.floor: 15pt is the floor, not a starting point: it is Apple's .subheadline size, still a Dynamic Type style, so it scales with the user's setting. Nothing here is a fixed px font size and nothing goes below it.
$meta.platform: iPhone / PWA-narrow: size floor 15pt, bubble is the measure. Mac / PWA-wide: size ceiling 16pt, measure capped at `measure` so a wide window does not produce 120-character lines. The tokens are one fluid set rather than three because the clamp() already lands on the right value at each width — a platform fork here would be three things to keep in sync.
$meta.contrast: Reply body is `text-primary`; reply metadata is `text-secondary`. Both are now checked against every ground a reply can sit on — `surface`, `agent-quiet` (quoted tool output), `accent-quiet` (your own turn) and `sunken` (code) — in section 2.2.

$meta.grid: 4pt. Every gap, pad and inset is a multiple of 4; nothing in the system uses an odd number.

$meta.note: Hit targets follow the HIG minimum of 44x44pt on touch; 28pt is the macOS pointer minimum.
Dark mode raises a surface by lightening it, not by casting a bigger shadow (HIG Dark Mode). Every level therefore pairs a shadow with a surface token and a hairline.

2.use: menus, popovers, the command palette, the model picker

3.use: sheets and modals over a scrim

$meta.note: Motion explains a change of state and nothing else. Under prefers-reduced-motion every duration collapses to `instant` and transforms become opacity cross-fades (HIG Motion / Reduced Motion criteria).
